title: Naturality and basis properties of explicit bounded coefficient scalars and geometric fibers
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and let $X$ be a scheme with noetherian underlying topological space [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For every scheme $T$, let $A_T=p_T^*\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] and let $F_\ell(|T|)$ be its finite-subextension-valued continuous function ring [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Fix the following explicit constructions, independent of any module presentation. The canonical finite-extension continuous-realization isomorphisms, normalized on every profinite test function, induce by filtered colimit a ring-object isomorphism $c_T:A_T\simeq(F_\ell)^{\#}_T$. Let $s_T:F_\ell(|T|)\to\operatorname{End}_{A_T}(A_T)$ be multiplication on the bounded-function presheaf, monoidally sheafified and transported through $c_T$. At a point $x\in T$, pull back to $\operatorname{Spec}(\overline{\kappa(x)})$, evaluate at the terminal object, use the coefficient identification obtained from $c$, the invertible bounded-presheaf unit at an algebraically closed field, and evaluation of a constant function, and turn the resulting internal abelian-group module into an ordinary $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-module by its tensor action. This defines $E_{T,x}$ and its regular-module coordinates $e_{T,x}$. These constructions and their additive and finite-colimit properties are proved in the module. The remaining assertion consists of four properties. (1) For every affine weakly etale $U\to X$ [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism] whose terminal-object evaluation takes every epimorphism of set sheaves on $U_{\mathrm{Proet}}$ to a surjection, $s_U$ is surjective. (2) For weakly etale $V\xrightarrow{g}U\to X$, normalized condensed coefficient inverse image, conjugated by its specified regular-module comparison, carries $s_U(a)$ to $s_V(a\circ g)$. (3) For every $x\in U$ and bounded $a$, $e_{U,x}(E_{U,x}(s_U(a))(e_{U,x}^{-1}(1)))=a(x)$. (4) If $U\to X$ and $V\to X$ send $x$ and $y$ to the same point, the functors $E_{U,x}\circ(U\to X)^*$ and $E_{V,y}\circ(V\to X)^*$ on all internal $A_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] are naturally isomorphic. There is no presentation, matrix, cover of another scheme, rank, local constancy or local freeness assertion in these coefficient properties.

proof.text: For a finite family of affine objects, finite_coproduct_evaluation supplies a site coproduct W, its comparison with the scheme coproduct, and the restriction bijection for every set sheaf. Apply that bijection to the sheaf of all continuous PadicAlgCl-valued functions. Restrictions of bounded functions are bounded, so injectivity follows from injectivity for continuous functions. For surjectivity glue the underlying continuous functions, choose a finite subextension E_i bounding each summand, and take their finite supremum. Scheme.sigmaMk and the coproduct comparison show every point of W belongs to a summand; therefore the glued function takes values in that supremum. For an empty family its supremum is the base field and the point condition is vacuous. This proves bounded_coproduct_bijective.

proof.text: Use the already proved general unit_iso_of_refinement implementation helper of the weakly contractible sheafification module. It applies to any abelian presheaf admitting the finite restriction-product comparisons on weakly contractible affines. Provide these comparisons for boundedP using the previous step: bijectivity constructs an inverse for the restriction fan in types; the forgetful functor from abelian groups reflects the resulting limit. The helper refines the image and equalizer sieves of the sheafification unit by finite affine contractible covers, splits their covering coproduct map using weak contractibility, combines representatives by the restriction-product bijection, and pulls back along the splitting. Thus the bounded-presheaf sheafification unit is an isomorphism on the given affine weakly contractible object. This uses the general proved helper, not a claim that boundedP is a point Kan extension.

proof.text: At the terminal object of the small site of Y, lift the image of the sheafified unit under an arbitrary regular-module endomorphism through the bounded-presheaf unit isomorphism. Let a be the underlying bounded function. Mod.bijective_one_comp_hom makes equality of regular-module maps equivalent to equality after the ring unit. Sheaf.unit_hom_ext and the monoidal sheafification adjunction identify that unit with the presheaf unit followed by toSheafify. A morphism out of the constant integer presheaf is determined by one at the terminal object: naturality along the unique map to that object determines one everywhere, and integer linearity determines every value. Finally toSheafify_naturality for boundedMul and one_mul show that sheafified multiplication by a has exactly the chosen image of one. This proves sheafScalar_surjective. Full restriction of scalars and the specified regular-module isomorphism transport this surjectivity through globalCoefficientIso to condensedQbarScalar_surjective.

proof.text: The arbitrary-scheme scalar pullback theorem gives the weakly etale restriction clause directly. At an algebraically closed field, identify the regular vector corresponding to one through the coefficient realization and the bounded unit. Naturality of the bounded multiplication map with the sheafification unit gives the value a at its unique point. The folded regularScalarValue composition and conjugation formulas transport this calculation along the chosen geometric point; scheme residue-field point evaluation gives a(x).

proof.text: For f:Y -> X and x in Y, the residue-field map makes the chosen algebraic closure of kappa(x) an algebraically closed extension of kappa(f(x)). IsAlgClosed.lift embeds the chosen algebraic closure of kappa(f(x)) in it over the base residue field. The two geometric-point morphisms then commute with f by Scheme.Hom.SpecMap_residueFieldMap_fromSpecResidueField. Whisker the field-extension evaluation isomorphism and compose the canonical upperStarComp comparisons. This yields fiber_X(f(x)) ~= f^* followed by fiber_Y(x). For two points with equal base image, compose the first comparison inverse, the equality-induced base-fiber isomorphism, and the second comparison. No common overfield is needed.
